newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel chemical industry sees 4 pct growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Israel chemical industry sees 4 pct growth in 1997.

text.p: Israeli chemical industry officials said on Wednesday they expect industry revenues from domestic production to grow by just four percent this year to $7.3 billion.
They said the slow growth was due the industry investing increasingly in production abroad, a phenomenon that led to a decline of about one percent in exports last year.

"There is a clear trend towards increased production and expansion of investments in companies abroad," said Akiva Moses, head of the Manufacturers Association's chemicals and pharmaceuticals division.
"For this reason we witnessed a decline for the first time in years in the chemical industry's exports," he told reporters at a news conference.

He said he expected export growth to be renewed this year but estimated it would be just two percent. Moses estimated the sale of Israeli chemical products manufactured abroad would grow by 10 percent.
Israel's chemical and pharmaceutical industries account for 14 percent of the country's industrial production.
Moses said the government's decision to cut subsidies for capital spending and its monetary policies were hurting the industry's performance.

"The government's monetary policy -- the frozen exchange rate, the high interest rates -- makes it hard for us to be competitive. It doesn't help our situation in terms of expenses and profits," he said.
Since the end of 1993, the dollar has gained only about 11 percent on the shekel, well under the domestic rate of inflation, which many analysts and business leaders blame on high interest rates.
